forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged down 23→22%. Late-June signals are mixed: Anthropic's formal OSTP submission reiterates it expects 'powerful AI' in late 2026/early 2027, and labs continue shipping frontier models roughly every ~11 days. But ARC-AGI-3 results show frontier models scoring under 1% on general-agent tasks, underscoring a wide remaining gap, and no lab has declared 'AGI' nor have 3+ leading researchers converged on it. The resolution bar remains unmet; small downward nudge on the benchmark evidence.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving within a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry optimism incentives. Such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Anthropic 'powerful AI' late 2026-2027; Altman within the term) sit inside the window
Cadence of frontier releases (~7 SOTA models Feb-Apr 2026) signals rapid capability gains

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
ARC-AGI-3 shows frontier models near 1% on general-agent tasks, exposing remaining gaps

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally declare 'AGI' rather than avoiding the term
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved' before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 25%. Fresh reporting confirms McKinsey cutting ~10% of its workforce (3,000-4,000 roles) attributed to AI productivity, with Bain/BCG/Deloitte making similar adjustments and ~25% of McKinsey fees now outcome-based. But BCG is actually growing headcount (tilted to AI/tech specialists), and the cuts so far concentrate in back-office, not a ≥33% revenue or employment collapse. The structural pressure is real but far below the resolution threshold; no change.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: established professional-services sectors suffering ≥33% revenue/employment decline within ~6 years from a single technological cause. Historically rare; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: Documented AI-driven cuts (~10% at McKinsey) and shift to outcome-based pricing compressing billable hours
Clients automating work previously outsourced, putting projects on hold amid excess capacity

factors_down.factor: BCG growing headcount overall; firms repricing rather than shrinking, blunting a revenue collapse
≥33% is a severe bar attributable primarily to AI by 2+ credible analyses within ~4 years

key_uncertainties: Whether AI substitution outpaces firms' ability to reprice and move up the value chain
Whether any decline would be cleanly attributed to AI rather than a broader demand cycle
update_triggers: Revise UP if a major firm reports double-digit revenue decline explicitly tied to AI
Revise DOWN if sector revenue/headcount proves resilient through 2027-2028

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 6%. Late-June polling is unchanged in shape: PollCheck's 7-poll average (27 Jun) has Reform ~26%, Labour ~21%, Conservatives ~19%; YouGov (21-22 Jun) has Reform 25%, Con 20%, Lab 18%, Grn 15%, LD 14%. Labour sits second or third with a fragmenting left (Green retention pulling votes). With the next GE not due until 2029 there is time to recover, but the current standing is poor; no change.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties trailing by ~5pp at roughly mid-term recovering to win most seats. Possible but a minority of cases; base ~25-30%, adjusted down for an unusually fragmented multi-party field.

factors_up.factor: Years remain before the GE (due by 2029) for economic and political conditions to shift
First-past-the-post can convert a modest Labour vote share into most seats in a split field

factors_down.factor: Labour second/third in current polling with approval near historic lows
Reform's sustained lead and left-vote leakage to Greens narrow Labour's path

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead proves durable or is a mid-term protest spike
How vote splits translate into seats under FPTP with four-to-five-way competition
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour returns to a polling lead or Reform's support visibly fades
Revise DOWN if Labour's deficit widens further or a leadership crisis erupts

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 83%. The 10-year horizon comfortably accommodates lab timelines (Anthropic 'powerful AI' 2026-2027; broad insider expectation of transformative AI within the decade) and the current rapid release cadence. The main drag remains definitional — whether a credible 'AGI' declaration or 3+ researcher consensus actually materialises — plus visible gaps such as sub-1% ARC-AGI-3 scores. No new information shifts the long-horizon view.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert-and-insider forecasts of transformative AI arriving within a ~9-year window. Aggregated expert surveys cluster around 50-70% for this horizon; lab insiders higher.

factors_up.factor: Decade-long window absorbs near-term slippage; multiple labs targeting transformative AI well inside it
Sustained compute scaling and rapid model cadence support continued capability gains

factors_down.factor: Resolution requires an explicit 'AGI' declaration or 3+ researcher consensus, which may never crystallise
Possible scaling plateau or unforeseen technical bottlenecks over a decade

key_uncertainties: Whether 'AGI' is ever formally declared rather than dissolving into incremental capability claims
Whether scaling and algorithmic progress hold up across the full decade
update_triggers: Revise UP if an AGI declaration or clear researcher consensus emerges
Revise DOWN if progress plateaus or labs retreat from AGI framing

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 7%. AEI's late-June China-Taiwan updates show the PLA rehearsing blockade mechanics (Coast Guard covering the Strait, Navy the eastern approaches), publishing mock strikes on Taiwanese LNG terminals, and demonstrating hypersonic and carrier-sustainment capability. But analysts (AEI, ASPI) judge a 2026 blockade/invasion unlikely, expecting continued grey-zone coercion rather than kinetic action; Trump-Xi talks yielded no Taiwan agreement. Capability signalling is rising without an imminent-action signal; no change.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: great-power initiations of a major blockade or amphibious assault against a defended territory within a fixed ~3.5-year window. Such initiations are rare; base ~5-8%.

factors_up.factor: Escalating PLA blockade rehearsals, LNG-terminal targeting, and hypersonic/carrier demonstrations
No diplomatic off-ramp from the Trump-Xi summit on Taiwan

factors_down.factor: Analyst consensus that 2026 is not the year; Beijing favours coercion short of kinetic action
Massive economic and military costs of a blockade/invasion deter initiation

key_uncertainties: Whether grey-zone pressure escalates into a >72hr blockade within the window
How US deterrence posture and cross-strait politics evolve through 2029
update_triggers: Revise UP if the PLA mobilises for a sustained blockade or major exercises shift to live operations
Revise DOWN if cross-strait tensions ease or credible deterrence is reinforced

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 1%. ONS data show CPI at 2.8% in the 12 months to May 2026, unchanged from April. Food and housing services are easing, but transport inflation accelerated sharply to 6.8% (highest since Dec 2022) on fuel, air fares and VED. With only ~6-7 monthly readings publishable before 1 Jan 2027 and the rate stuck near 2.8%, a fall below 2.0% in any one month is highly unlikely; no change.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional base rate: probability headline CPI drops >0.8pp to breach a sub-2.0% print within ~6 months from a sticky 2.8% with upward transport pressure. Very low; ~1-3%.

factors_up.factor: Food and household-services disinflation continuing (food at lowest since Dec 2024)
Possible sharp energy/fuel price reversal or downside data surprise

factors_down.factor: Headline stuck at 2.8% with transport inflation surging to 6.8%
Few remaining monthly prints before the deadline leave little room for an >0.8pp fall

key_uncertainties: Whether energy/fuel prices fall sharply enough to drag headline below 2.0%
Whether services inflation decelerates faster than currently projected
update_triggers: Revise UP if a monthly print drops toward ~2.2% with momentum still falling
Revise DOWN if inflation reaccelerates above 3%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 91%. Pre-release tracking continues to strengthen: best US first-day presales in five years, >$40M domestic presales, and projections of a $200M+ (potentially $250M+) domestic opening — the biggest since Deadpool & Wolverine — ahead of the 31 July release. The comparison point, No Way Home, reached $1.9B. The $1.5B bar is high but the franchise pedigree and record presales make it the central case; no change pending actual opening figures.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: tentpole superhero sequels with record presales and a marquee franchise. The subset clearing $1.5B worldwide is select but Spider-Man's flagship entries cluster near/above it; base ~55-65%, adjusted up for exceptional tracking.

factors_up.factor: Direct precedent: No Way Home grossed ~$1.9B; strong cultural-event positioning

factors_down.factor: $1.5B worldwide is a high absolute bar few films reach
Opening hype can fade with weak word-of-mouth or a soft international run

key_uncertainties: Actual opening weekend and multiplier once the film releases 31 July
update_triggers: Revise UP after a record opening with strong reviews and legs
Revise DOWN if the opening underwhelms or word-of-mouth is poor

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 99%. Mid-2026 reporting already puts Anthropic at roughly $30-47B annualized (Sacra ~$47B in May; Anthropic-cited ~$30B run rate) and OpenAI around $33B (May), implying a combined ~$63-80B now — already at or above the threshold on most estimates, and both are growing fast. Reaching a combined >$70B by Q4 2026 is near-certain barring a methodology dispute knocking figures down; no change.
forecasts.base_rate: Near-deterministic given current run-rates and trajectory; this is an extrapolation, not a genuine uncertainty, so the estimate sits at the >95% calibration ceiling.

factors_up.factor: Combined annualized revenue already ~$63-80B by May 2026 on credible estimates
Both firms compounding rapidly (Anthropic ~30x in 15 months)

factors_down.factor: ARR accounting disputes (OpenAI contests Anthropic's figure by ~$8B) could trim the reported sum
Tail risk of a demand shock or reporting gap by Q4 2026

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition the most credible Q4 2026 reporting adopts
Whether any reporting lag leaves Q4 figures ambiguous at resolution
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only if both firms' growth sharply reverses or reporting is revised down materially

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 38%. The OBR's March 2026 outlook implies aggregate potential output growth around ~1.5% (medium-term productivity ~1% plus labour-supply growth falling toward ~0.5% by 2030), with AI adding ~0.2pp to productivity by the horizon; per-person growth is just 1.1% to 2030. The IFS is slightly more upbeat at ~1.4% average. The 1.5% decade-average threshold sits right at the central estimate, so it is close to a coin-flip tilted below; no change.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: UK decade-average real GDP growth exceeding 1.5%. The 2010s averaged roughly 2% but post-2016 trend growth has slumped toward ~1.2-1.5%; base ~35-45% for the coming decade.

factors_up.factor: AI-driven productivity uplift (OBR ~0.2pp by horizon; IFS sees potential growth rising)
Investment/consumption recovery could lift growth above trend mid-decade

factors_down.factor: Falling labour-supply growth from lower migration and ageing caps potential output
Persistent weak productivity trend and fiscal headwinds; OBR potential growth ~1.5% or below

key_uncertainties: Whether the AI productivity boost materially exceeds the OBR's cautious ~0.2pp assumption
The net path of migration, participation and ageing on labour supply through the 2030s
update_triggers: Revise UP if productivity data or AI diffusion durably beat OBR assumptions
Revise DOWN if trend productivity or labour supply deteriorates further
